$$
\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|

\qquad \text{for all }x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d.
$$
This controls changes in the gradient, not changes in the function value itself.

evidence_excerpts: If $f$ is $L$-smooth, then, for every $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d$,

$$
f(y)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle
+\frac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2.
$$
This is a quadratic upper bound. Its inequality points upward from the right-hand model to $f(y)$: reversing the sign would give a different statement.
